note: A green arrow means you have a protected movement in the direction of the arrow, but you must still yield to any vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection and to pedestrians lawfully in the crosswalk. Once the way is clear, you should proceed in the direction of the arrow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is a primary danger of excessive speed?
options: a:Saves time getting to your destination.,b:Increases the chance of severe injury or death.,c:Reduces tire wear.,d:Helps you maneuver around obstacles.
note: Excessive speed greatly increases both your stopping distance and the force of any impact, which makes crashes more likely to cause severe injury or death. Even small increases over a safe speed can dramatically raise crash severity while usually saving very little travel time.

question: Which statement about work zones is correct?
options: a:Work zones have no special rules.,b:You must slow for designated work or Cone Zones and expect higher fines.,c:Slow only if you think workers are present.,d:Fines are the same as for normal driving and you only slow when workers are visible.
note: Work zones require extra caution. You must obey all work-zone signs and reduced speed limits, including “Cone Zone” or similar warnings. Many states impose higher fines for violations in work zones to protect road workers and other drivers, whether or not workers are visibly present.

question: Which behavior might identify an aggressive driver?
options: a:Driving under the posted speed limit.,b:Having many passengers in the vehicle.,c:Erratic and improper lane changes.
note: Aggressive drivers often follow too closely, speed, and make sudden or improper lane changes. Erratic lane changes increase crash risk because other drivers cannot predict their movements, so you should give such drivers extra space.

question: For best control when turning quickly, how should your hands be positioned on the steering wheel?
options: a:Next to each other at the top of the wheel.,b:One hand at the top and one at the bottom.,c:On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
note: Keeping your hands on opposite sides of the wheel (around the 9-and-3 or 8-and-4 positions) gives you the best leverage and control, especially for quick or sharp turns. This position helps you steer smoothly and react safely at higher speeds.

question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you at night, what is the safest action to take?
options: a:Glance toward the right edge of the road until the vehicle passes.,b:Switch to your high beams to judge distance.,c:Turn your lights on and off to get their attention.,d:Close your eyes briefly until the glare passes.
note: When oncoming headlights blind you, avoid looking directly at them. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane and use the road markings as a guide. This keeps you in your lane and reduces glare while maintaining safe control of the vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement is true about driving too slowly?
options: a:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.,b:The speed you drive has no effect on safety.,c:Driving too slowly is never unsafe.
note: Driving much slower than the flow of traffic can be dangerous because faster vehicles may need to brake or change lanes suddenly, increasing the risk of rear-end and sideswipe collisions. Use posted minimum speeds where they exist and avoid unnecessarily obstructing traffic.

question: In which situation should your wheels not be pointed straight ahead?
options: a:When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.,b:When waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light.,c:When parked on the side of a level roadway with no curb.,d:When stopped at a red light.
note: When parking on a hill, you should turn your wheels so that if the vehicle rolls, it will move toward the curb or edge of the road, not into traffic. Pointing the wheels straight ahead on a slope can allow the vehicle to roll directly into the roadway if the brakes fail.

question: If you feel fatigued while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Increase the radio volume to stay alert.,b:Increase your speed to reach your destination faster.,c:Find a safe place to pull over and take a short nap.
note: If you start to feel drowsy, the safe choice is to get off the road and rest. Turning up the radio or trying to push through fatigue does not restore alertness and greatly increases your risk of a crash.

question: When you want to change lanes, which action should you never do?
options: a:Signal well before changing lanes.,b:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.,c:Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.,d:Move into another lane while within an intersection.
note: You should never change lanes while you are in the middle of an intersection because traffic movements are more complex and less predictable there. Instead, signal early, check mirrors and blind spots, and complete the lane change before or after the intersection when it is safe.

question: What should you do when you encounter a deep puddle on the roadway?
options: a:Maintain the posted speed to drive through it.,b:Shift into neutral before entering the puddle.,c:Avoid the puddle if possible.
note: Deep puddles can hide potholes, debris, or uneven pavement and can cause hydroplaning. If you can safely avoid the puddle, do so. If you must drive through water, slow down and proceed cautiously to maintain control.

question: If your vehicle is struck from the rear, which action should you avoid?
options: a:Pressing your head against the headrest.,b:Be ready to apply brakes and keep a firm grip on the wheel.,c:Letting go of the steering wheel.
note: If your vehicle is struck from the rear, keep both hands on the steering wheel and press your head firmly against the head restraint. This helps you maintain control of the vehicle and reduces the risk of neck injury. Never let go of the steering wheel in a rear-end collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, when should you move back into the right lane?
options: a:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:As soon as you feel like it.,c:When you are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.,d:When you are one vehicle length ahead of the passed vehicle.
note: After passing, do not move back into the right lane until you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough space ahead of that vehicle and reduces the risk of cutting them off.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer signals you to stop despite a green traffic light, what must you do?
options: a:Obey the officer’s directions.,b:Follow the traffic signal instead of the officer.,c:Ignore both and proceed with caution.,d:Do what the vehicle ahead of you does.
note: When a police officer is directing traffic, their hand signals and commands override traffic lights and signs. Even if the light is green, you must follow the officer’s directions and stop, because they may be managing a hazard, collision, or special situation.

question: How can you avoid becoming an aggressive driver yourself?
options: a:Relax and allow extra time so you are not rushed.,b:Tailgate slower drivers to encourage them to speed up.,c:Drive above the posted limit to keep up with traffic.,d:Honk frequently to express frustration.
note: To avoid becoming an aggressive driver, stay calm, allow extra travel time, and focus on safety instead of “winning” in traffic. Do not tailgate, speed, or try to punish other drivers; these behaviors increase crash risk and can escalate conflicts.

question: Only which factor can reduce BAC and alcohol’s effects on the body?
options: a:Time for the body to eliminate alcohol.,b:Taking vitamin supplements.,c:Eating fatty foods before driving.,d:Drinking caffeinated beverages.
note: Only time lowers your blood alcohol concentration. Your body must metabolize the alcohol; coffee, food, cold showers, or vitamins do not make you sober faster and do not make it safe to drive.

question: When should drivers set the parking brake?
options: a:Only in parking lots.,b:Only when parked on a steep hill.,c:Every time they park.
note: You should set the parking brake every time you park, on hills and on level ground. This helps keep the vehicle from rolling if the main parking mechanism fails. With a manual transmission, leave the car in gear; with an automatic, leave it in Park.

question: A broken yellow line down the center of the road signals what?
options: a:A construction zone ahead.,b:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,c:Passing is permitted from either direction.
note: A broken yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions and indicates that passing is allowed from either direction when it is safe. You must still check for oncoming traffic and ensure you have enough clear distance before crossing the line.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:Into the second lane always.,b:Into any lane if it is safe.,c:Into the first available lane of the one-way street.
note: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, you must turn from the lane nearest the centerline into the first available legal lane on the one-way street. This keeps your path short and predictable and prevents you from cutting across multiple lanes, which can cause conflicts with other traffic.

question: If your vehicle becomes disabled on the highway, where should you park if possible?
options: a:Stop in the travel lane where you broke down.,b:Stop in the right lane and leave hazards off.,c:Park on any nearby shoulder even if partly blocking traffic.,d:With all four wheels off the traveled portion of the roadway.
note: If your vehicle becomes disabled, you should move it as far off the traveled portion of the roadway as possible, ideally with all four wheels off the road. This reduces the risk of being hit by passing traffic and gives other drivers more room and time to react.

question: Why is night driving more hazardous?
options: a:Distance and speed are harder to judge in the dark.,b:There are always fewer cars on the road at night.,c:Vehicles travel faster at night.
note: Night driving is more hazardous mainly because you cannot see as far or as clearly. Headlights limit how much of the road you can see, making it harder to judge how far away other vehicles or objects are and how fast they are moving. This reduced visibility increases the risk of mistakes and collisions.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:When it may help prevent a collision.,b:When you are angry at another driver.,c:To get other drivers moving in a traffic jam.
note: Use your horn as a safety tool, not to show anger. It is appropriate to use the horn to warn other road users when they might not see you or when a collision could occur, such as if another driver starts to move into your lane. Avoid using it to express frustration or to hurry other drivers.

question: For drivers under 21, a blood alcohol concentration of what level can lead to license suspension?
options: a:0.08 percent or higher.,b:Any detectable amount of alcohol.,c:0.15 percent or higher.
note: South Dakota has zero tolerance for drivers under 21; any detectable alcohol can result in penalties including a two-year license suspension.

question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Four-way flashers only.
note: In fog, always use low beam headlights. High beams shine light higher and can reflect off the water droplets in the fog, creating glare and making it harder to see. Low beams aim light down toward the road and improve your ability to see lane lines and the edge of the roadway. Four‑way flashers do not help you see ahead and should not replace proper headlight use.

question: If no crosswalk is present and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and allow the pedestrian to finish crossing.,b:Honk and continue slowly.,c:Ensure the pedestrian can see you before proceeding.,d:Cautiously drive around the pedestrian.
note: If a pedestrian is in your lane, you must yield, even if there is no painted crosswalk. The law generally treats many places as “unmarked crosswalks,” especially at intersections, and drivers must stop or slow as necessary to let pedestrians cross safely. Honking, edging forward, or driving around a pedestrian in the roadway is unsafe and can easily cause a crash.

question: What term describes the amount of alcohol in a person's blood?
options: a:Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).,b:Implied consent (IC).,c:Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).
note: Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) is the standard term for the amount of alcohol in a person’s blood. It is usually expressed as a percentage, such as 0.08%. As BAC increases, judgment, reaction time, and coordination are increasingly impaired, which greatly raises crash risk.

question: Tailgating (driving too close to the rear bumper ahead) can:
options: a:Never result in a traffic citation.,b:Frustrate other drivers and lead to unsafe behavior.,c:Reduce collisions by preventing cars from cutting in.
note: Tailgating can provoke aggressive reactions and lead to collisions; it can also result in citations for following too closely.

question: How far ahead should you be scanning the roadway while driving to avoid sudden maneuvers?
options: a:About ten seconds ahead.,b:About four seconds ahead.,c:About seven seconds ahead.
note: Good defensive driving means looking well ahead, not just at the vehicle in front of you. Scanning about 10 seconds ahead gives you time to see slowing traffic, curves, and other hazards early so you can change lanes or adjust speed smoothly instead of making sudden, risky maneuvers.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim headlights, where should you look?
options: a:Directly at the approaching headlights so you can judge distance.,b:Toward the center line to maintain course.,c:Down at your dashboard until they pass.,d:Toward the right side of the road to avoid glare.
note: When an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, avoid looking directly into the glare. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane or the right side of the road and use the lane markings or road edge as a guide. This reduces temporary blindness from the bright lights while helping you maintain a safe path.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you avoid entering an intersection even if the light is green?
options: a:Only if you entered on a yellow light earlier.,b:If police are directing traffic elsewhere.,c:If you know you will block the intersection when the light turns red.,d:You may enter as long as the light is green regardless of congestion.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless there is enough space for your vehicle to completely clear it, even if the light is green. If traffic is backed up and you would end up stopped in the intersection when the light changes, you must wait behind the stop line. Blocking the intersection can prevent cross traffic and emergency vehicles from moving safely.

question: As you approach the crest of a hill, how should you prepare?
options: a:Maintain the same speed regardless of visibility.,b:Be prepared to stop if necessary and reduce speed as needed.,c:Speed up slightly to clear the hill faster.
note: As you approach the top of a hill, your view of what is ahead is limited. There may be a stopped vehicle, an animal, a pedestrian, or a slow-moving car just over the crest. Reduce your speed and be ready to stop if needed so you can react safely to any hazard that appears suddenly beyond the hill.

question: How do stopping distances and crash severity change with vehicle speed?
options: a:Crash severity decreases as speed increases because of momentum.,b:Both stopping distance and crash severity increase as speed increases.,c:Speed has no effect on stopping distance or crash severity.,d:Stopping distance decreases with speed.
note: As speed increases, your vehicle needs more distance to come to a complete stop because both reaction distance and braking distance grow. Crash severity also increases with speed because the energy released in a collision rises rapidly as speed goes up. Driving slower when conditions require it gives you more time and space to avoid or lessen a crash.

question: A broken yellow line between two lanes of traffic means:
options: a:Both lanes of traffic are going in the same direction.,b:Passing is not permitted.,c:Passing is permitted when it's safe.,d:The lane is for buses only.
note: A broken (dashed) yellow line between lanes means traffic is moving in opposite directions and passing is allowed when it is safe. You may cross the line to pass another vehicle only if you have enough clear sight distance, there is no oncoming traffic close enough to be a hazard, and passing is not otherwise prohibited by signs or conditions.

question: When passing another vehicle, what is the recommended approach?
options: a:Honk continuously while passing to warn them.,b:Pass as safely and as quickly as possible then return when clear.,c:Match the other vehicle’s speed and stay alongside for several seconds.,d:Pass as slowly as possible to reduce noise.
note: When passing, you should move into the passing lane, accelerate to pass promptly without exceeding the speed limit, and minimize the time you spend beside the other vehicle. Return to your lane only when you can see the passed vehicle in your mirror and it is clearly safe. Do not honk continuously or linger alongside the other vehicle.

question: On an interstate, how can you best avoid vehicles merging from on-ramps to your right?
options: a:Change lanes to the left when traffic permits.,b:Maintain your current speed and position in the right lane.,c:Slow down or speed up slightly, if needed, to create a safe gap for merging vehicles.
note: On multi‑lane highways, the safest way to help merging traffic is to move to the left lane when it is safe, giving entering vehicles a clear space to merge. If you cannot change lanes safely, adjust your speed slightly to create a gap, but do not stop or make abrupt moves that could surprise other drivers.

question: How can you encourage the driver behind you to keep a safe distance?
options: a:Brake abruptly to create space.,b:Maintain a steady speed.,c:Drive 10 mph faster than the car behind you.,d:Drive 10 mph slower than the car behind you.
note: Maintaining a steady speed and signaling early for turns or lane changes helps drivers behind you judge distance and adjust their following space. Avoid sudden braking or large speed changes, which can cause tailgaters to get even closer or lead to rear‑end collisions.

question: How should you make room for vehicles entering a freeway?
options: a:Speed up to pass the merging vehicle quickly.,b:Maintain your speed and position without yielding.,c:Stop on the shoulder to let them in.,d:Change lanes or adjust your speed to allow them to merge.
note: Freeway traffic should cooperate with vehicles using the on‑ramp. If possible, change lanes away from the merge area or adjust your speed slightly so a clear gap opens for the entering vehicle. Do not stop on the freeway or race the merging vehicle; smooth, predictable adjustments keep traffic flowing safely.

question: Why should you leave extra following distance behind large vehicles?
options: a:Because other drivers tend to pull behind large vehicles before passing.,b:Because it keeps you from being caught in the vehicle’s slipstream.,c:To better see around the vehicle and because the driver may not see you.
note: Large vehicles block your view of the road ahead and have larger blind spots, so their drivers may not see you if you follow too closely. Leaving extra following distance improves your ability to see traffic conditions and gives you more time to react if the large vehicle brakes or swerves.

question: What are work zone or construction signs usually like in appearance?
options: a:Square or rectangular with white background and red symbols.,b:Round or octagonal with black and yellow markings.,c:Diamond-shaped or rectangular with an orange background and black symbols.
note: Work zone and construction signs are temporary warning signs. They are typically diamond-shaped or rectangular with an orange background and black letters or symbols, alerting drivers to road work and the need to slow down and use extra caution.

question: When a school bus has red flashing lights, when may vehicles proceed?
options: a:As soon as all students are off the bus.,b:When the stop arm is retracted but the bus remains stopped.,c:Only after the bus's red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is retracted.
note: When a school bus has red flashing lights and the stop arm extended, traffic in most situations must stop because children may be crossing the road. You may proceed only after the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is retracted, indicating that children are no longer boarding or exiting and it is safe to move. The safest practice is to wait until the bus’s signals are off and it is clear that children are out of the roadway.

question: If your car begins to skid, what should you avoid doing with the brakes?
options: a:Pump the brakes repeatedly.,b:Apply the brakes lightly.,c:Use the brakes only after you regain control of the skid.
note: If your car begins to skid, you should stay off the brakes. Braking hard can lock the wheels and make the skid worse. Instead, ease off the accelerator and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go until you regain traction. Once the vehicle is back under control, you can brake gently if needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a roadway marked with a single broken white centerline, what is allowed?
options: a:You must stay in your lane and never cross.,b:You may cross the line to change lanes when safe.,c:You may change lanes only from the left lane.
note: A single broken white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross a broken white line to change lanes or pass when it is safe and legal to do so, after checking mirrors and blind spots and signaling your intention.

question: If stopped for a traffic violation, which documents must you present?
options: a:Only your license.,b:Only your insurance and registration.,c:Your driver's license, vehicle registration, and proof of insurance.
note: If you are stopped for a traffic violation, you are generally required to show three documents: your valid driver’s license, the vehicle’s current registration, and proof of insurance. These documents show that you are legally allowed to drive and that the vehicle is properly registered and insured.

question: You park downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way do you turn the front wheels?
options: a:Toward the side of the road (right).,b:Toward the center of the road (left).,c:Straight ahead.
note: On a downhill slope with no curb, turn your front wheels toward the edge of the road (to the right). If the vehicle rolls, it will move off the roadway instead of into oncoming traffic.

question: What is the purpose of rumble strips along the roadway?
options: a:To test a vehicle's shock absorbers.,b:To alert drivers to potential tire problems.,c:To warn inattentive drivers through vibration and sound that they are leaving the travel lane.,d:To provide extra traction in wet weather.
note: Rumble strips are grooved or raised patterns on the road that cause vibration and noise when driven over. They are designed to warn inattentive or drowsy drivers that they are leaving their lane or approaching a hazard, such as a stop sign or work zone.

question: Which of these factors affects how alcohol is absorbed by an individual?
options: a:Intelligence.,b:Weight.,c:Height.,d:Clothing color.
note: A person’s body weight is one of the main factors that affects how quickly alcohol is absorbed and how strongly it affects them. Heavier individuals generally have more body water to dilute alcohol. Other factors include biological sex, food in the stomach, and how much and how quickly alcohol is consumed.

question: When may you legally drive around or under a lowered railroad crossing gate?
options: a:When you can see clearly both directions.,b:When warning lights are not flashing.,c:Never.
note: It is illegal and extremely dangerous to drive around or under a lowered railroad crossing gate. You must wait until the lights stop flashing, the gate is fully raised, and you have checked that the tracks are clear before crossing.

question: When passing a row of parked vehicles, what should you be prepared for?
options: a:All other drivers and pedestrians to respect your right-of-way.,b:A person or vehicle unexpectedly entering your lane.,c:That it is safe to hug the parked vehicles to allow more traffic space.,d:To keep speed constant and maintain distance.
note: When passing parked vehicles, leave space and be ready for doors opening, pedestrians stepping out, or a vehicle pulling away from the curb. Expect that someone or something may suddenly enter your lane and adjust your speed and position so you can react safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To turn left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, which lane should you start from?
options: a:The center lane of the road.,b:Any lane as long as it’s safe.,c:The lane closest to the left curb.
note: On a one-way street, a left turn must start from the lane closest to the left curb. This keeps you in the proper path for turning and avoids cutting across other lanes of traffic.

question: On a dimly lit street at night, what speed should you choose?
options: a:Keep instrument panel lights bright to be more visible.,b:Drive at the posted speed regardless of visibility.,c:Slow enough to stop within the distance illuminated by your headlights.,d:Use high beams so you can see farther without slowing.
note: At night or in low light, you must drive slowly enough that you can stop within the distance you can see ahead with your headlights. If you overdrive your headlights, you may not have enough time or space to stop for hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another car, when do you have enough room to return to your lane?
options: a:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:After you look over your shoulder once.,c:When the other driver signals for you to re-enter the lane.
note: After passing, you should not move back into your original lane until you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror. This indicates you have enough space to return without cutting the other driver off.

question: For drivers 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a minimum BAC of:
options: a:0.10 percent.,b:0.05 percent.,c:0.02 percent.,d:0.08 percent.
note: In South Dakota and most U.S. states, it is illegal for drivers 21 and older to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher. Even lower levels can still impair driving, but 0.08% is the per se legal limit.

question: Truck blind spots are located:
options: a:On the immediate left of the cab and directly behind the truck.,b:On both sides of the truck and directly behind it.,c:Directly behind the truck only.
note: Large trucks have sizable blind spots directly behind them and along both sides, especially on the right and close to the cab on the left. If you cannot see the truck driver’s face in the side mirror, the driver likely cannot see you, so avoid lingering in these areas.

question: If pedestrians are crossing imprope rly (not in a crosswalk), what must you do?
options: a:You must stop for them.,b:You do not have to stop for them.,c:Honk your horn to make them move.,d:Drive around them carefully.
note: Even if pedestrians are crossing outside a crosswalk, you must slow or stop as needed to avoid hitting them. Drivers are required to exercise due care and yield to pedestrians already in the roadway to prevent a collision.

question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, which headlight setting is appropriate?
options: a:Keep your headlights on low beam so you don’t blind the driver ahead.,b:Use high beams until you are within 10 feet of the vehicle ahead.,c:Turn off your lights to be less distracting.,d:Use fog lights only.
note: When following another vehicle at night, use low‑beam headlights so your lights do not shine directly into the mirrors of the driver ahead. High beams can cause glare and make it harder for that driver to see.

question: Which statement about large trucks is correct?
options: a:Large trucks are more maneuverable than passenger cars.,b:Large trucks require more distance to stop than passenger vehicles.,c:Large trucks are exempt from traffic laws regarding stopping distances.,d:All large trucks have brakes that allow quick stops similar to cars.
note: Because of their greater size and weight, large trucks need more time and distance to stop than passenger cars traveling at the same speed. You should never cut closely in front of a truck or assume it can stop as quickly as a smaller vehicle.

question: When making a left turn, which action should you avoid?
options: a:Signaling to other drivers.,b:Cutting the corner.,c:Slowing down before the turn.,d:Turning into the wrong lane.
note: When turning left, you should slow down and signal well in advance, then turn into the correct lane without cutting the corner. Cutting the corner can put you into the path of oncoming traffic or vehicles in adjacent lanes, creating a serious collision risk.

question: How often should you check your rearview mirrors while driving?
options: a:Often,b:Only when you want to check a blind spot.,c:Only when you are slowing down.,d:Only when changing lanes.
note: You should check your mirrors frequently—about every few seconds—to stay aware of traffic behind and beside you. Regular mirror checks help you spot fast‑approaching vehicles, lane changes, and potential hazards early, rather than only when slowing or checking blind spots.

question: What does a curb painted red indicate?
options: a:The area is reserved for quick pick-up or drop-off.,b:No stopping, standing, or parking at any time (except to obey traffic controls or officers).,c:Loading zone only.
note: A red curb means no stopping, standing, or parking at any time, except when required to obey a traffic control device or officer. It is used for emergency access or other strict no‑stopping zones, not for loading or quick drop‑offs.

question: Driving significantly slower than surrounding traffic is generally:
options: a:A good idea if the weather is bad.,b:Often a hazard because it may cause others to pass unsafely.,c:Appropriate if you don’t know the speed limit.
note: Driving much slower than surrounding traffic can be dangerous because faster drivers may make sudden lane changes or risky passing maneuvers to get around you. You should generally travel at the speed of traffic, as long as it is within the posted limit and safe for conditions.

question: How many alcoholic drinks are enough to impair your driving ability?
options: a:Three drinks are needed to affect you.,b:Two drinks are required before impairment.,c:One drink can affect your driving.
note: Even one alcoholic drink can slow your reactions and affect your judgment, vision, and coordination. Because you cannot reliably know how much alcohol will impair you, the safest choice is not to drive after drinking at all.

question: If another vehicle cuts in front of you dangerously close, what is the best immediate action?
options: a:Take your foot off the gas to increase space.,b:Honk and brake hard.,c:Swerve into the adjacent lane suddenly.
note: If a vehicle cuts in too closely, the safest response is to ease off the accelerator to create more following distance. Avoid sudden braking or swerving, which can cause a rear‑end collision or loss of control.

question: To reduce the chance of hydroplaning during rain, you should:
options: a:Put on cruise control to maintain speed.,b:Move to the shoulder as soon as it starts raining.,c:Decrease your speed.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on a thin layer of water and lose contact with the road. Slowing down in the rain, especially when water is pooling, greatly reduces this risk. Avoid cruise control on wet roads so you can adjust speed quickly if you start to lose traction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a one-way street, when may you turn left onto another one-way street?
options: a:Only if traffic moves to the right on the street you're entering.,b:If you increase your speed before the turn.,c:When traffic on the street you are turning onto moves to the left.
note: On a one‑way street, you may turn left onto another one‑way street only when traffic on the street you are entering is moving to the left and there is no sign prohibiting the turn. Always signal, move into the left lane before turning, and yield to pedestrians and other traffic.

question: When a red light is displayed but a green arrow points the way, when may you proceed?
options: a:Only after coming to a complete stop first.,b:Only after the red light changes to green.,c:If you are in the proper lane, the intersection is clear, and you yield to pedestrians and any traffic already in the intersection.
note: A green arrow means you have a protected movement in the direction of the arrow, even if the circular red light is on. You may proceed in the direction of the arrow only if you are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear, but you must still yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and any vehicles already in the intersection.

question: When you see a school crossing sign, how should you respond?
options: a:Watch for children and be prepared to stop.,b:Always sound your horn when you see children.,c:Increase speed to clear the crossing quickly.,d:Always stop even if no stop sign is present.
note: A school crossing or school zone sign means you must slow down, watch carefully for children, and be prepared to stop. Children may enter the roadway unexpectedly, so use extra caution and follow any posted reduced speed limits or crossing‑guard directions.

question: If another driver is passing you in a no-passing zone, what should you do?
options: a:Pull off the road to make more room.,b:Maintain your speed and position to allow the other driver to re-enter safely.,c:Speed up to prevent being passed.,d:Brake abruptly to prevent the pass.
note: If another driver is passing you, even in a no‑passing zone, keep a steady speed and stay in your lane so the driver can complete the pass and return safely. Do not speed up or brake suddenly, as this can cause a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is a U-turn prohibited?
options: a:On a straight roadway with clear visibility for 500 feet both ways.,b:On or near any curve or hill.,c:In a parking lot.
note: You must not make a U‑turn on or near a curve or hill where you cannot see far enough ahead to be sure it is safe. Limited visibility makes it hard to judge oncoming traffic and can lead to serious head‑on collisions.

question: If bad weather reduces visibility, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to clear the area quickly.,b:Increase your following distance.,c:Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
note: When visibility is reduced by rain, fog, or snow, you need more time to see hazards and react. Increasing your following distance gives you extra space to brake smoothly and avoid sudden maneuvers if the vehicle ahead slows or stops.

question: If your vehicle begins to hydroplane, what action should you take?
options: a:Apply the brakes firmly to regain traction.,b:Maintain speed to drive through the water quickly.,c:Slow down gradually and avoid braking.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water and lose contact with the road. Ease off the accelerator and let the vehicle slow down gradually. Avoid hard braking or sudden steering, which can cause a skid and further loss of control.

question: When following a large truck on the freeway, where should you position your vehicle?
options: a:Farther behind the truck than you would follow a passenger vehicle.,b:Directly to the right of the truck at all times.,c:Closer behind the truck than behind a passenger vehicle.,d:In the truck's blind spot to improve aerodynamics.
note: Large trucks need more distance to stop and have big blind spots directly behind them. Stay farther back than you would behind a car so you can see the truck’s mirrors and have enough space to react if it slows or stops suddenly.

question: Which headlights should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Four-way flashers only.,c:Low beam headlights.
note: In fog, use low beam headlights (and fog lights if your vehicle has them). High beams reflect off the fog and create glare, making it harder to see. Low beams aim light down toward the road and improve your ability to see lane lines and vehicles ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you required to stop your vehicle?
options: a:Only when directed by traffic signs and not officers.,b:Only at a red light but not for officers.,c:When another driver waves you down.,d:Whenever a police officer orders you to stop or at a red traffic light.
note: You must always stop when a police officer orders you to and at a steady red traffic light, unless specifically directed otherwise by an officer. Law enforcement directions override traffic signals and signs for safety and traffic control.

question: What does a steady green traffic light at an intersection mean?
options: a:Adjust your mirrors then proceed.,b:Increase your speed to clear the intersection immediately.,c:You may proceed through the intersection when the way is clear and it is safe to do so.
note: A steady green light means you may go straight or turn, but only if the intersection is clear and it is safe. You must still yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any vehicles already in the intersection or lawfully within the intersection oncoming traffic when turning left.

question: Like alcohol and drugs, what effect can drowsiness have on driving?
options: a:Improve reaction time.,b:Impair your judgment.,c:Help you become more alert.,d:Have no effect at all.
note: Drowsiness makes you less alert, slows your reaction time, and impairs your judgment, similar to alcohol or drugs. A drowsy driver may not notice hazards in time or may make poor decisions, greatly increasing the risk of a crash.

question: When is hand-over-hand steering the recommended technique?
options: a:During normal driving on straight roads or gentle curves.,b:When backing straight or making small adjustments for controls.,c:When making sharp turns at low speed, such as tight corners or parking maneuvers.
note: Hand‑over‑hand steering is best for sharp, low‑speed turns, such as turning at tight intersections, parking, or making U‑turns. It lets you turn the wheel quickly and with control. For normal driving and small steering corrections, use a push‑pull (shuffle) technique; when backing straight, keep one hand on the top of the wheel and turn smoothly rather than using full hand‑over‑hand.

question: After a minor, non-injury intersection collision with little damage, what should you do if possible?
options: a:Never move your vehicle under any circumstances.,b:Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane.,c:Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until police arrive.
note: After a minor crash with no injuries and drivable vehicles, you should move your car out of the traffic lane if it is safe to do so. This helps prevent additional collisions, keeps traffic flowing, and allows you to exchange information in a safer location.

question: If you must park where parking is not normally provided, what should you ensure?
options: a:Park five feet from the curb.,b:Park with your reverse lights on.,c:Leave the engine running.,d:Make the vehicle visible to drivers approaching from any direction.
note: If you must park where parking is not normally provided, make sure your vehicle is clearly visible to other drivers from all directions. Use your hazard lights if appropriate and avoid blocking traffic or creating a surprise obstacle, so other drivers have time to see and safely react to your parked vehicle.

question: How should you behave when driving through a construction zone?
options: a:Stop to watch the workers.,b:Pass carefully and avoid slowing to look at the work.,c:Decrease your following distance to clear the zone faster.
note: In construction zones you should drive slowly and carefully, follow posted work‑zone speed limits, and avoid rubbernecking. Slowing just to look at the work distracts you and can cause sudden braking and rear‑end crashes. Keep your attention on the road, workers, and traffic control devices so you can react safely.

question: A driver license is considered which of the following?
options: a:A privilege that can be revoked.,b:A mandatory possession for all citizens.,c:A guaranteed civil right.
note: A driver license is a privilege granted by the state, not a guaranteed right. You must meet requirements such as passing tests and obeying traffic laws to keep it. The state can suspend or revoke your license for violations like DUI, excessive points, or driving without insurance.

question: If a vehicle is about to hit you from the rear, which action should you avoid?
options: a:Brace yourself by pressing your back and head against the seat and head restraint.,b:Release your seat belt.,c:Hold the steering wheel firmly and be ready to apply brakes.
note: If you are about to be hit from the rear, keep your seat belt fastened, press your back and head firmly against the seat and head restraint, and hold the steering wheel tightly. This helps reduce whiplash and keeps you in control of the vehicle. Never release your seat belt in a crash situation.

question: Before changing lanes or passing, what steps should you take?
options: a:Check mirrors, look over your shoulder for blind spots, and signal before changing lanes or passing.,b:Honk to warn drivers instead of signaling.,c:Rely solely on your mirrors and omit a head check.,d:Signal only after you start to move into the other lane.
note: Before changing lanes or passing, you must check your mirrors, look over your shoulder to check blind spots, and signal in advance. Mirrors alone do not show vehicles in your blind spots, and signaling only after you start moving does not give others enough warning. Use your horn only if needed to avoid a collision, not as a substitute for proper signaling and observation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you have oncoming vehicles to your left and parked vehicles to your right, which path should you steer?
options: a:Closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.,b:Directly onto the shoulder.,c:A middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles.,d:Closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming vehicles.
note: When you have oncoming traffic on one side and parked vehicles on the other, steer a middle course. This gives you the most space from both hazards. Staying too close to oncoming vehicles increases head‑on crash risk, and staying too close to parked cars increases the chance of hitting a door or a car pulling out.

question: How does a BAC of 0.02 percent affect accident risk?
options: a:It nearly doubles the driver’s chance of a crash.,b:It only affects drivers under 21.,c:It makes you immune to impairment.,d:It has no effect on driving ability.
note: Even a small amount of alcohol in your system can affect judgment, reaction time, and coordination. Studies show that crash risk begins to rise at low BAC levels, and around 0.02% BAC the risk of being in a crash is already noticeably higher than at 0.00%. You should never assume a low BAC is “safe” for driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should the maximum posted speed limit be driven?
options: a:Only during the night.,b:Only during the day.,c:Under ideal conditions.
note: The posted speed limit is the maximum speed allowed under ideal conditions—good visibility, dry pavement, light traffic, and a safe vehicle. When conditions are less than ideal, such as in rain, fog, heavy traffic, or poor road surfaces, you are required to slow down to a speed that is safe for those conditions, even if it is below the posted limit.

question: When changing lanes, what should you do to check for traffic in your blind spot?
options: a:Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.,b:Rely only on the left side mirror.,c:Sound your horn before moving.,d:Rely only on the rearview mirror.
note: Before changing lanes, you must check your mirrors and then quickly look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move. This shoulder check lets you see into the blind spot—areas your mirrors cannot show—so you don’t move into a lane already occupied by another vehicle.

question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you should always look:
options: a:Only behind you to check for following traffic.,b:Only ahead and rely on signals.,c:To the left and right sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.
note: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you must scan to both the left and right to see if vehicles, trains, pedestrians, or cyclists are approaching. Looking both ways before proceeding helps you spot hazards early and avoid collisions with traffic entering from the sides.

question: Which road surface is most likely to be icy after snow or rain on cold days?
options: a:Residential streets that get sun.,b:Major highways with traffic.,c:Open hilly roads.,d:Roads in shaded areas.
note: Roads in shaded areas stay colder and do not dry as quickly as roads in the sun. After snow or rain on cold days, these shaded spots can remain icy even when other parts of the road look clear, so you should be especially cautious when driving through shaded curves, under bridges, or in tree-covered areas.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer directs you to go through a red light without stopping, what should you do?
options: a:Stop until the light turns green.,b:Come to a complete stop before proceeding.,c:Ignore the officer and obey the traffic signal.,d:Follow the officer's direction and go through the intersection.
note: When a police officer is directing traffic, their hand signals and instructions legally override traffic lights and signs. You must follow the officer’s directions, even if that means proceeding through a red light, as long as you can do so safely.

question: Any amount of alcohol in the bloodstream can impair a driver's:
options: a:Right-of-way privileges.,b:Judgment and physical coordination.,c:Knowledge only.
note: Any amount of alcohol can affect the parts of your brain that control judgment, reaction time, and coordination. Even if you do not feel drunk, your ability to make safe driving decisions and control the vehicle can be impaired.

question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?
options: a:After you start moving the vehicle.,b:Only when you need them while driving.,c:Before you begin driving.
note: Before you start driving, you should adjust your seat, steering wheel, and all mirrors so you have a clear view around your vehicle. Doing this while stopped prevents distraction and ensures you are ready to drive safely once the vehicle is moving.

question: When is highway pavement most slippery after rain begins?
options: a:One to two hours after it starts raining.,b:After it has been raining several hours.,c:Right when it first starts to rain.
note: When rain first begins, water mixes with oil and other residues on the road surface, creating a very slick layer. Until the rain has washed these substances away, traction is reduced and the pavement is especially slippery.

question: Because motorcycles and scooters are harder to see, you should:
options: a:Share a lane with the motorcycle.,b:Slow only when behind them.,c:Make constant visual checks and be especially alert.
note: Motorcycles and scooters are smaller and can be easily hidden in blind spots or by other vehicles. You should check mirrors and blind spots frequently, look carefully before changing lanes or turning, and give motorcycles a full lane just as you would any other vehicle.

question: If you approach a stopped school bus with flashing lights and its signal arm extended, you must:
options: a:Proceed at normal speed but watch for children.,b:Stop and remain stopped until the bus resumes motion and signals are retracted.,c:Proceed at 15 mph if no children are visible.
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is retracted. In most situations on an undivided road, this applies to drivers in both directions. Only on some divided highways with a physical median are opposing-direction drivers not required to stop.

question: When a centerline consists of double solid yellow lines, what is the passing rule?
options: a:No passing from either direction.,b:Passing permitted if no oncoming traffic.,c:Passing permitted from the left only.,d:Passing permitted from the right only.
note: Double solid yellow lines indicate that passing is prohibited in both directions because traffic moves in opposite directions and visibility is limited.

question: When changing lanes, which action should you avoid?
options: a:Checking for other vehicles that may move into the same lane.,b:Looking over your shoulder to check your blind spot.,c:Changing lanes abruptly or without signaling.,d:Using your turn signal to alert others.
note: Never change lanes suddenly or without signaling; check mirrors and blind spots to ensure the lane is clear.

question: In foggy conditions, what is the proper driving action?
options: a:Slow down and use low beam headlights.,b:Turn on high beam headlights to cut through the fog.,c:Increase speed to get through the fog faster.,d:Turn on interior dome lights.
note: Slow your speed and use low beams; if visibility is extremely poor, pull safely off the road and wait for conditions to improve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection where all corners have stop signs, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver who arrived before you.,b:The driver across from your vehicle.,c:The driver on your left.,d:If two or more vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.
note: At a four-way stop, the vehicle that arrives first has the right-of-way and should proceed first after stopping. If two or more vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. Always communicate with signals and proceed cautiously, making eye contact if needed.

question: If you see heavy smoke covering the roadway ahead, what should you do?
options: a:Turn on your high beams and continue driving.,b:Slow down, move as far right as possible, and stop off the roadway if needed.,c:Turn on your four-way flashers and proceed.
note: When heavy smoke covers the roadway, you should slow down, move as far to the right as you safely can, and stop off the roadway if possible. Turn on your low‑beam headlights and, if stopped, your hazard flashers so others can see you. Do not drive into thick smoke at normal speed because you may not see stopped vehicles, debris, or other hazards in time to avoid a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When your view of cross traffic at an intersection is blocked, how should you proceed?
options: a:Slow down briefly and look both directions without stopping.,b:Stop,c:Keep your speed and look both ways.
note: If your view of cross traffic is blocked at an intersection, you must come to a complete stop. After stopping, inch forward slowly until you can clearly see traffic on the cross street. Only enter the intersection when you are sure it is safe and there are no vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians in your path.

question: What do 'No passing zone' signs indicate to drivers?
options: a:To maintain a steady speed only.,b:To slightly increase your speed.,c:That it is unsafe and illegal to pass in the marked area.
note: A 'No passing zone' sign tells you that passing is both unsafe and illegal in that area. These zones are placed where you cannot see far enough ahead or where road conditions, such as hills, curves, or intersections, make passing dangerous. You must stay in your lane and not overtake other vehicles until you are past the no‑passing zone.

question: What should you do with loose objects inside your vehicle?
options: a:Leave them on the floor near the driver’s seat.,b:Secure them so they won’t become hazards in a sudden stop.,c:Put them in the passenger seat to watch over them.,d:Place them on the dashboard for easy access.
note: Loose objects inside a vehicle can become dangerous projectiles in a sudden stop or crash and can also roll under pedals or interfere with steering. Always secure items in the trunk, cargo area, or storage compartments so they cannot move around while you are driving.

question: You may cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle if:
options: a:The vehicle in front moves to the right to let you pass.,b:The opposite side has a broken yellow line but the line next to your lane is solid.,c:You have a broken yellow line next to your lane and enough clear distance to pass safely.,d:The road is clear for a long distance but the line next to your lane is solid.
note: Yellow center lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. You may only cross to pass when the yellow line next to your lane is broken, and only if you have enough clear distance ahead to pass safely without exceeding the speed limit. If there are double solid yellow lines, or the solid line is on your side, you must not cross to pass.

question: How dangerous is backing your vehicle?
options: a:Dangerous only if you have a helper guiding you.,b:Only dangerous in large vehicles.,c:Always dangerous.
note: Backing is always risky because your view to the rear and sides is limited, and it is harder to see pedestrians, small children, and obstacles. You should avoid backing when possible, back slowly, check mirrors and blind spots, and use a helper when available.

question: If your vehicle develops a mechanical problem while driving, what is the best course of action?
options: a:Signal and move into the slow lane.,b:Keep driving until you find a service station.,c:Put on your hazard lights and pull off the road away from traffic.,d:Stop in your lane and put on your hazard lights.
note: If your vehicle has a mechanical problem, you should signal, move off the roadway to a safe place away from traffic if possible, and turn on your hazard lights so other drivers can see that your vehicle is disabled. Staying in a traffic lane or continuing to drive a failing vehicle can create a serious hazard.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering the interstate on a short ramp with no acceleration lane, what should you do?
options: a:On the ramp, adjust your speed so you can enter the interstate only after identifying a safe gap in traffic.,b:Immediately enter the far-right lane and then speed up.,c:Use the shoulder of the main road to get up to speed.,d:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a police signal.
note: On a short entrance ramp with no acceleration lane, you must judge traffic on the interstate, wait for a safe gap, and then accelerate on the ramp so you are near the speed of traffic as you merge. Do not use the shoulder or stop at the end of the ramp unless traffic conditions leave you no other safe option.

question: What does a steady red arrow pointing right mean at an intersection?
options: a:You must stop and may not turn in that direction until the signal changes.,b:You may turn after making a complete stop.,c:You may turn only if no pedestrians are present.,d:You may turn after slowing and yielding to traffic.
note: A steady red arrow means you must come to a complete stop and you are not allowed to proceed in the direction of the arrow until a green arrow or green light allows movement. Treat it like a red light specifically for that turning movement.

question: How can sudden wind gusts on highways affect drivers?
options: a:They affect some vehicles more than others, but can be hazardous to all drivers.,b:They only cause visibility problems.,c:They can cause problems for all vehicles.
note: Sudden wind gusts can push any vehicle sideways, making it harder to stay in your lane, and can blow dust or debris that reduces visibility. Larger and lighter vehicles are often affected more, but all drivers should be prepared to steer smoothly and reduce speed if necessary.

question: If a child is bicycling near your vehicle, you should:
options: a:Assume the child is in total control of the bicycle.,b:Expect the unexpected and be prepared for sudden moves.,c:Beep your horn to get their attention.
note: Children on bicycles can be unpredictable and may suddenly swerve, stop, or enter your lane without warning. You should slow down, give them extra space, and be prepared to react quickly rather than assuming they are fully in control or using your horn, which could startle them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you legally pass another vehicle?
options: a:When you are on a hill or curve with good visibility.,b:When a solid line is next to your driving lane.,c:When there is a broken yellow line next to your lane and it is safe to pass.,d:At a railroad crossing.
note: You may pass another vehicle only when it is both legal and safe. A broken yellow line next to your lane means you are allowed to pass if you have enough clear distance ahead and no oncoming traffic. Passing is not allowed where there is a solid yellow line next to your lane, at railroad crossings, or on hills/curves where you cannot see far enough ahead.

question: Approaching an intersection with a flashing red light, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop,b:Slow down and yield only if necessary.,c:Proceed without stopping if no one else is present.,d:Wait for the light to turn green before moving.
note: A flashing red light is treated the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, yield the right-of-way as needed, and proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe to go.

question: Large trucks are most likely to lose speed when:
options: a:Driving down long gradual hills.,b:Driving up long or steep hills.,c:Driving in long, heavy traffic.
note: Large trucks are heavy and require a lot of power to climb. On long or steep uphill grades, they usually slow down significantly because it takes more effort to pull their weight uphill. When driving near trucks on hills, expect them to lose speed on the way up and give them extra space to change gears or maintain lane position.

question: If a tire blows out, what immediate action should you take?
options: a:Apply the brake hard immediately.,b:Pull over immediately without slowing gradually.,c:Hold the steering wheel firmly and slow down gradually.
note: When a tire blows out, the key is to stay in control of the vehicle. Grip the steering wheel firmly to keep the vehicle going straight, ease off the accelerator, and let the car slow down gradually. Avoid hard braking, which can cause a skid. Once you have slowed and the vehicle is stable, steer carefully to the side of the road and stop in a safe place.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching an intersection with a steady yellow light and not already in the intersection, you should:
options: a:Proceed without slowing.,b:Ignore the signal and follow the vehicle ahead.,c:Speed up to beat the red light.,d:Stop safely if you can do so.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. If you are not yet in the intersection, you must stop if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop without hard braking or skidding, continue through carefully and clear the intersection before the light turns red.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After completing a pass, when is it safe to return to your driving lane?
options: a:When you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:After signaling for at least three seconds.,c:When the other driver signals you to return to the lane.
note: After passing, you should not move back into your original lane until you can see the front of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror, not its headlights. Seeing the entire front of the vehicle in your mirror shows you have enough space to return without cutting the other driver off.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to your original lane?
options: a:When you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:After you have just cleared the front bumper of the passed vehicle.,c:When you are a safe distance ahead of the passed vehicle and have checked your mirrors and blind spot.,d:When the passed vehicle flashes its headlights or otherwise signals you to return.
note: When you pass another vehicle, stay in the passing lane until you are well ahead. A good rule is to wait until you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Then signal, check your blind spot, and return to your lane when it is safe, without forcing the other driver to slow down.

question: At a railroad crossing you must:
options: a:Proceed without stopping if you don't see a train immediately.,b:Only look for a single train approaching.,c:Drive faster to clear the tracks quickly.,d:Watch for vehicles required to stop at all railroad crossings and for multiple trains.
note: At railroad crossings, you must approach with caution, be prepared to stop, and never assume only one train is coming. Some vehicles, such as school buses and certain hazardous-materials trucks, must always stop at all railroad crossings. Multiple tracks can have more than one train approaching, so always look and listen carefully before crossing.

question: If you experience a tire blowout, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down gradually and use the brakes lightly.,b:Apply the brakes firmly and immediately.,c:Pump the brakes to slow quickly.
note: With a tire blowout, hold the steering wheel firmly, ease your foot off the accelerator, and let the vehicle slow down gradually. Use the brakes lightly only after you have good control and your speed has dropped. Braking hard or suddenly can cause you to lose control, especially if a front tire has blown.

question: Before you enter an intersection, where should you look?
options: a:Only to the left once.,b:Down at the instrument panel.,c:Left,d:Only to the right.
note: Before entering an intersection, scan in all directions: look left first (because cross‑traffic from the left is closer), then right, then left again, and quickly ahead. This pattern helps you spot vehicles, pedestrians, or hazards that may enter your path from any side.

question: Why should drivers give children on bicycles extra space?
options: a:They always use bike lanes correctly.,b:They are smaller and may ride unpredictably.,c:They drive faster than adults.
note: Give children on bicycles extra space because they are smaller and harder to see, and they often ride unpredictably or make sudden moves without signaling. Extra distance and lower speed give you more time to react if they wobble, swerve, or enter your lane unexpectedly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering traffic you should do what first?
options: a:Only watch the vehicle ahead of the gap.,b:Speed up and force other vehicles to make room.,c:Check behind you and to the sides before entering the gap.
note: When entering traffic, first check behind you and to the sides to be sure there is a safe gap and that no one is quickly approaching in the lane you plan to enter. After confirming it is clear, adjust your speed to match traffic and merge smoothly without forcing others to brake hard.

question: What must drivers do when a school bus is loading or unloading children?
options: a:Slow down and be ready to stop but not necessarily stop.,b:Pass the bus cautiously if no children are crossing.,c:Come to a complete stop when the bus has red lights flashing and stop arm extended, as required by law.,d:Stop only if you are traveling in the same direction as the bus on a divided highway (rules vary by state).
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, drivers in both directions must stop on undivided roads. Remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and children are safely out of the roadway. On a divided highway, only traffic traveling in the same direction as the bus must stop, unless state law says otherwise.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you drive slower than the normal flow of traffic, you will most likely:
options: a:Interfere with traffic and possibly receive a ticket.,b:Demonstrate defensive driving techniques.,c:Improve traffic flow.
note: Driving much slower than the normal flow of traffic can cause other drivers to brake or change lanes suddenly, increasing the risk of collisions. If you must drive below the flow, stay in the right lane when possible and use turnouts where available so faster traffic can pass.

question: A flashing red traffic signal at an intersection requires you to:
options: a:Come to a complete stop,b:Reduce your speed and proceed with caution.,c:Proceed as if it were a flashing yellow light.,d:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped while it flashes.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, look for traffic and pedestrians, yield the right‑of‑way as needed, and then proceed only when it is safe.

question: In heavy fog, what lighting should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Emergency flashers only.
note: In fog, use low beam headlights (and fog lights if your vehicle has them). High beams reflect off the fog and create glare, which makes it harder to see the road and other vehicles.

question: Which foot should you use for both the brake and accelerator?
options: a:Use your left foot to brake.,b:Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.,c:Always brake abruptly to stop quickly.
note: For normal passenger vehicles, you should use your right foot for both the accelerator and the brake. This helps prevent pressing both pedals at once and allows smoother, more controlled stops.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle using its flashing lights, what must you do?
options: a:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.,b:Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until it passes.,c:Maintain your speed and stay in your lane.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using lights and siren, you must yield the right‑of‑way by pulling over to the right edge of the road and stopping. Stay stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed and it is safe to reenter traffic.

question: If a pedestrian with a guide dog is at a corner ready to cross before you make a right turn, what must you do?
options: a:Tell the pedestrian when it is safe to cross.,b:Proceed if you think you can beat them across.,c:Turn off your engine until they finish crossing.,d:Wait until the person has crossed before turning.
note: A pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane has the right‑of‑way. You must wait until the person has completely crossed the street before making your turn, giving them extra time and space for safety.

question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line indicate?
options: a:Passing is permitted only from the lane next to the solid line.,b:Passing is permitted in both directions.,c:Passing is prohibited in both directions.,d:Traffic next to the broken line may pass; traffic next to the solid line may not.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only for traffic on the side with the broken line. Drivers next to the solid yellow line must not cross it to pass. This marking separates traffic moving in opposite directions and controls where passing is safe.

question: Why is driving at night generally more hazardous than daytime driving?
options: a:The road is always more slippery at night.,b:Your reaction time is always slower at night.,c:You cannot see as far ahead at night.
note: Night driving is more hazardous mainly because you cannot see as far ahead. Headlights provide limited range, and glare from other vehicles can further reduce visibility. With less time to see and react to hazards, the risk of collisions increases, even if road and driver conditions are otherwise the same.

question: When you see pedestrians near the roadway, how should you respond?
options: a:Sound your horn and maintain speed.,b:Speed up to clear the area quickly.,c:Slow down and pass with caution.
note: When pedestrians are near the roadway, you should slow down, be prepared to stop, and pass with great caution. Pedestrians can change direction or step into the road unexpectedly, and drivers are required to yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and when they are close to the lane of travel.

question: If you want to enter a freeway but there is no gap in traffic, what should you do on the ramp?
options: a:Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap so you can accelerate to traffic speed.,b:Stop at the end of the ramp until traffic clears.,c:Force other drivers to make space by maintaining ramp speed.
note: On a freeway entrance ramp, you should use the ramp and acceleration lane to reach the speed of freeway traffic and merge into a safe gap. If there is no gap, you must be prepared to slow or stop at the end of the ramp if necessary, yielding to freeway traffic. Never force your way in or assume others will move for you.

question: When a school bus on your side of the road has its red lights flashing, what is required of you?
options: a:Slow to a speed no faster than 10 mph.,b:Proceed once the students have moved away from the bus.,c:Change lanes and pass cautiously.,d:Stop until the lights stop flashing.
note: When a school bus on your side of the road has red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn. This protects children who may be crossing the road and may be hard to see around the bus.

question: How close to a fire hydrant are you prohibited from parking?
options: a:Within 30 feet.,b:Within 15 feet.,c:Within 20 feet.
note: You must not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant so firefighters can quickly connect hoses in an emergency. Leaving this space clear ensures emergency vehicles can access the hydrant without delay.

question: How should you check your vehicle's blind spots?
options: a:By looking only in your side mirrors.,b:By turning your head and glancing over your shoulder.,c:By checking only your rearview mirror.,d:By relying on rear sensors only.
note: Mirrors alone do not show areas directly alongside and slightly behind your vehicle. To check blind spots, quickly turn your head and glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move before changing lanes or merging.

question: To reduce glare from oncoming headlights, where should you briefly look?
options: a:Stare at the centerline of the road.,b:Toward the right side of the road.,c:Flash your high beams to warn the other driver.
note: Bright oncoming headlights can temporarily blind you. To reduce glare, briefly look toward the right edge of your lane and use it as a guide, then return your eyes to scanning the road ahead once the vehicle passes.

question: When parallel parked facing downhill, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn the wheels away from the side of the road.,b:Turn the wheels to the left only.,c:Turn the wheels sharply toward the side of the road (toward the curb).,d:Keep the wheels straight.
note: When parking facing downhill with a curb, turn your front wheels sharply toward the curb. If your brakes fail, the vehicle will roll into the curb instead of into traffic.

question: When crossing a sidewalk to enter traffic from a driveway or alley, what should a driver do?
options: a:Stop before driving onto the sidewalk area.,b:Expect pedestrians on the sidewalk to yield.,c:Stop only if pedestrians are present.,d:Honk to warn pedestrians.
note: When crossing a sidewalk from a driveway or alley, you must stop before the sidewalk and yield to all pedestrians. Only proceed when the sidewalk is clear and it is safe to enter the roadway.

question: Which part of driving does alcohol affect first?
options: a:Only coordination initially.,b:Judgment and decision-making.,c:Balance before mental skills.,d:Vision before anything else.
note: Alcohol first affects judgment, reasoning, and decision‑making. A driver may feel more confident and take risks before obvious physical signs like poor coordination or blurred vision appear, which is why even small amounts of alcohol are dangerous for driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you and the driver on your left arrive simultaneously at a four-way stop, who goes first?
options: a:The driver on your right has the right-of-way.,b:The driver signaling a turn has the right-of-way.,c:You have the right-of-way.
note: At a four‑way stop, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This rule helps avoid confusion: always look to see who is on your right and allow that driver to go first when you arrive together.

question: Where should a driver direct their attention while driving?
options: a:Stare straight ahead at all times.,b:Focus only on the middle of the road.,c:Look only at the instrument panel.,d:Scan ahead, to the sides, and use your mirrors regularly.
note: Safe drivers constantly scan the road ahead, to the sides, and check mirrors regularly. This helps you spot hazards early, adjust speed or position, and avoid sudden surprises. You should not stare in one place; keep your eyes moving and look well ahead of your vehicle.

question: At about what speed can a car begin to hydroplane on wet pavement?
options: a:Around 35 miles per hour.,b:Around 45 miles per hour.,c:Around 40 miles per hour.
note: Hydroplaning can begin around 35 mph on wet roads, especially with worn tires or deeper water. As speed increases, your tires may ride up on a thin layer of water instead of gripping the pavement, causing a loss of steering and braking control.

question: Before stopping at a traffic light or sign, what should you do first?
options: a:Check your mirrors for surrounding traffic.,b:Press down hard on the accelerator.,c:Set the parking brake.
note: Before stopping, check your mirrors to see traffic behind and around you. Knowing what is happening behind helps you slow down gradually, signal in time, and avoid being hit from the rear by a driver who is not paying attention.

question: When descending a long or steep hill, what should you do regarding vehicles behind you?
options: a:Check your mirrors often for fast-approaching vehicles.,b:Hold the brake pedal down steadily to control speed.,c:Assume traffic behind you keeps a constant speed.
note: When driving downhill, gravity can cause both your vehicle and others to gain speed quickly. You should check your mirrors frequently so you know if a vehicle is approaching from behind too fast and can adjust safely. Do not assume traffic behind you will maintain a constant speed.

question: Which statement about drugs and driving is true?
options: a:Herbal supplements never affect driving ability.,b:Any prescription drug is safe to use if you don't feel drowsy.,c:Even over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.,d:Only illegal drugs can impair your driving.
note: Many medications, including over-the-counter drugs like cold medicine or allergy pills, can cause drowsiness, slow reaction time, or affect judgment. Any substance that impairs your ability to drive safely—whether prescription, over-the-counter, herbal, or illegal—can make it unsafe and unlawful to drive. Always read labels and follow medical advice before driving.

question: A broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line means passing is:
options: a:Not permitted from either side.,b:Permitted from the side next to the solid yellow line.,c:Permitted from the side next to the broken yellow line.,d:Allowed only during daylight.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only for traffic on the side with the broken line. If the solid line is on your side, you must not cross it to pass. Always pass only when you have enough clear distance and it is safe and legal to do so.

question: What is the safe condition to return to your lane after passing another vehicle?
options: a:When you cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.,b:When you have passed the other vehicle’s front bumper.,c:When you feel comfortable.,d:When you can see the other vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.
note: After passing, you should not move back into your original lane until you can clearly see the front of the vehicle you passed—usually its headlights—in your rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough space ahead of that vehicle and reduces the risk of cutting it off or causing a rear-end collision.

question: How must you respond to a flashing red traffic light at an intersection?
options: a:Stop only if other vehicles are present.,b:Come to a full stop,c:Slow down and go through if no cars are visible.,d:Wait for the light to turn green before proceeding.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, look for cross traffic and pedestrians, yield the right-of-way as needed, and proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe to go.

question: What does an orange-and-red triangular emblem on the back of a vehicle indicate?
options: a:The vehicle is carrying hazardous materials.,b:The vehicle has the right-of-way.,c:The vehicle is a slow-moving vehicle.,d:The vehicle is an emergency vehicle.
note: An orange-and-red triangular emblem is the universal symbol for a slow-moving vehicle, such as farm equipment or certain construction vehicles. It warns other drivers that the vehicle travels at lower speeds, so they should be prepared to slow down and pass only when it is safe.

question: What is the safest method for changing from one lane to another?
options: a:Change lanes quickly and often.,b:Change lanes gradually and carefully.,c:Only change lanes when another car is in your blind spot.,d:Always avoid changing lanes.
