note: The safest way to change lanes is to do it gradually and carefully: check mirrors, signal, check your blind spot, and then move smoothly into the new lane. Sudden or frequent lane changes increase the risk of collisions because other drivers have less time to see and react to your movements.

question: How should head restraints be positioned for maximum safety?
options: a:Set as low as possible behind the seat.,b:Removed if they feel uncomfortable.,c:Adjusted to contact the back of the occupant’s head.,d:Folded down when not in use.
note: Head restraints should be adjusted so the top is roughly level with the top of your head and the restraint is close to or lightly touching the back of your head. This position helps support your head and neck in a rear-end collision and reduces the risk of whiplash injuries.

question: If you experience a sudden tire blowout, what should you do first?
options: a:Pump the brakes repeatedly to slow down.,b:Apply the brakes as hard as possible immediately.,c:Turn the steering wheel sharply toward the shoulder.,d:Hold the steering wheel firmly and ease off the gas
note: In a sudden tire blowout, grip the steering wheel firmly to keep the vehicle going straight and immediately ease off the accelerator. Do not slam on the brakes. Once the vehicle slows and you have it under control, gently brake as needed and steer to a safe place off the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving at high speeds, how long before changing lanes or turning should you signal?
options: a:At least 100 feet before the turn or lane change (200 feet or more at higher speeds, such as on highways).,b:Only when you begin turning the steering wheel.,c:Two seconds before turning or changing lanes.,d:Signaling is optional at high speeds.
note: At higher speeds, you should signal well in advance so other drivers have time to see your intention and adjust. A good rule is to signal at least 100 feet before turning or changing lanes in most areas, and at least 200 feet (or more) when driving faster, such as on highways. Think in terms of distance rather than an exact number of seconds, because the time it takes to cover that distance changes with your speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic signal is not operating, how should you treat the intersection?
options: a:You may proceed if the intersection appears clear.,b:Obey only the stop lines and not other vehicles.,c:As an all-way stop; stop and yield before entering.,d:Drive quickly through to clear the intersection.
note: When a traffic signal is completely out, you must treat the intersection as an all‑way stop. Come to a full stop at the stop line or before the crosswalk, then proceed only after yielding to any vehicles or pedestrians who arrived first or are already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering an interstate highway from a ramp, you should:
options: a:Use the ramp and acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic and merge smoothly.,b:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a large gap.,c:Use the acceleration lane to match traffic speed, check for a safe gap, and merge smoothly.,d:Enter the highway at any speed as long as your turn signal is on.
note: When entering an interstate, use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic, check mirrors and blind spots, and merge into a safe gap without stopping. Stopping on the ramp or entering far below traffic speed is dangerous because other drivers do not expect a stopped or very slow vehicle at the end of the ramp.

question: After passing on the left, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: a:After about three seconds have passed.,b:When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.,c:When you can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.,d:As soon as you finish accelerating.
note: After passing another vehicle, do not move back into the right lane until you can see the front of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror. This shows you have enough space to return without cutting the other driver off and forcing them to brake suddenly.

question: Which headlights should be used when driving in fog, rain, or snow?
options: a:Parking lights only.,b:Fog lights only without beams.,c:High beam headlights.,d:Low beam headlights.
note: In fog, rain, or snow, always use low beam headlights. Low beams reduce glare and reflection from moisture in the air, helping you see the road and be seen by others. High beams reflect off fog, rain, or snow and can actually make it harder to see.

question: Which driving abilities are diminished by alcohol or drugs?
options: a:Reaction time, coordination, judgment, alertness, and concentration.,b:None; only vision is affected.,c:Only alertness and concentration.,d:Only alertness.
note: Alcohol and many drugs impair multiple driving abilities at the same time. They slow reaction time, reduce coordination, harm judgment, and weaken alertness and concentration. Because safe driving depends on all of these skills working together, any amount of impairment greatly increases crash risk.

question: When must you always stop before crossing railroad tracks?
options: a:Only when the crossing is in a city or town.,b:Only if you are transporting two or more young children.,c:If there isn't room on the other side for you to fully clear the tracks.
note: You must never stop on railroad tracks. Only proceed if there is enough space on the far side for your entire vehicle to clear the tracks completely. If traffic or obstacles prevent you from fully clearing the tracks, stop and wait before the tracks until you can cross safely.

question: Give the right-of-way to any pedestrian who is:
options: a:Only in any crosswalk or intersection.,b:Wearing bright clothing.,c:Crossing any street (in marked or unmarked crosswalks).,d:Only in a marked crosswalk.
note: Drivers must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians crossing the street in both marked and unmarked crosswalks at intersections. Even when a crosswalk is not painted, there is often a legal crosswalk at intersections, and you must be prepared to stop for pedestrians who are crossing there.

question: When driving in fog, which headlights should you use?
options: a:Interior lights for better visibility.,b:Parking lights only.,c:High beam headlights.,d:Low beam headlights.
note: In fog, use low beam headlights. Low beams aim light downward and reduce glare, helping you see the road and be seen by others. High beams reflect off the water droplets in fog and create more glare, which makes it harder to see.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes, how can you check your blind spot?
options: a:Use only the inside rearview mirror.,b:Turn your head and look over your shoulder into the lane you intend to enter.,c:Use only the side mirror.
note: Before changing lanes, always turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move. This quick glance checks the blind spot that mirrors cannot show, helping you avoid vehicles, motorcycles, or bicycles that may be alongside you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto the freeway, what speed should you aim for?
options: a:More slowly than freeway traffic.,b:At the legal speed limit regardless of traffic speed.,c:At or near the speed of the freeway traffic.
note: When merging onto a freeway, use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to reach a speed at or near the flow of freeway traffic, as long as you stay within the speed limit. Matching the speed of traffic allows you to merge smoothly and safely without forcing other drivers to brake suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a flashing yellow light at an intersection mean?
options: a:Come to a complete stop immediately.,b:Stop and proceed only when no vehicles are present.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down, look carefully in all directions, and proceed through the intersection only when it is safe. You are not required to stop, but you must be prepared to yield to pedestrians and other vehicles already in or close to the intersection.

question: When driving at night, you should:
options: a:Look directly at oncoming headlights to adjust.,b:Increase your following distance.,c:Always use your high beams.
note: At night your visibility is reduced, so you need more time and space to react. Increasing your following distance gives you extra room to stop or steer away from hazards you may not see until later. You should avoid looking directly at oncoming headlights and use high beams only when appropriate and dim them for oncoming traffic or when following another vehicle.

question: Having a driver license is considered a:
options: a:Privilege.,b:Public entitlement.,c:Requirement.,d:Right.
note: In all U.S. states, driving is a privilege, not a right. The state issues a driver license only when you meet certain requirements, and it can suspend or revoke that license if you violate traffic laws or drive unsafely.

question: Which of the following commonly contributes to traffic crashes?
options: a:Exceeding posted speeds or driving too fast for conditions.,b:Obeying traffic laws.,c:Getting adequate rest and staying alert.,d:Scanning the environment regularly.
note: Driving faster than the posted speed limit or too fast for road, traffic, or weather conditions greatly increases your stopping distance and crash risk. Safe drivers adjust their speed to match conditions and stay within the law, rather than simply driving as fast as other traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering traffic from a curbside parked position, what should you do?
options: a:Wait for a large enough gap so you can accelerate up to traffic speed before merging.,b:Drive more slowly than other traffic for 200 feet.,c:Wait for the first two vehicles to pass then enter in front of them.
note: When pulling out from a curb, you must wait for a gap large enough to signal, check mirrors and blind spots, and accelerate smoothly up to the speed of traffic without forcing other drivers to brake hard or swerve. Entering too slowly or cutting in front of close vehicles creates a hazard.

question: What is a driving distraction?
options: a:Anything that makes you pay more attention to driving.,b:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,c:Anything that causes evasive action only.
note: A distraction is any activity or object that diverts attention from driving and can lead to crashes.

question: How should you respond to a flashing yellow traffic light at an intersection?
options: a:Slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution.,b:Stop and wait for a green light before moving.,c:Increase your speed to clear the intersection quickly.,d:Ignore it unless pedestrians are present.
note: A flashing yellow light warns you to slow down, be alert, and proceed carefully through the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach a green light but the intersection is blocked by traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Enter and wait for traffic to clear while blocking the crosswalk.,b:Partially enter the intersection to hold your right-of-way.,c:Do not enter the intersection until you can get completely across.
note: Never enter an intersection unless you can clear it completely; blocking an intersection is illegal and dangerous.

question: How does driving on gravel or dirt roads affect traction and stopping?
options: a:Tires have less traction on gravel and dirt so you must slow down.,b:Tires grip the road better than on pavement.,c:Visibility is better than on pavement.,d:Stopping distance is shorter.
note: Loose gravel and dirt reduce tire traction compared to pavement; you must slow down because it takes longer to stop and skids are more likely.

question: When stopping on snow or ice in a vehicle with ABS, what is the correct braking method?
options: a:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.,b:Pump the brakes manually.,c:Stay off the brakes and let the vehicle drift to a stop.
note: Vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems require firm continuous pressure on the brake pedal; the system pulses the brakes automatically.

question: What is the best general method to avoid dangerous driving situations?
options: a:Be aware of everything happening around your vehicle.,b:Turn off the radio to eliminate distractions.,c:Keep your gaze fixed directly ahead at all times.
note: Being aware of everything happening around your vehicle is the foundation of defensive driving. You should constantly scan ahead, to the sides, and check your mirrors so you can spot hazards early and have time and space to react safely.

question: If a road is slippery, what following distance should you keep?
options: a:Farther from the car ahead than normal.,b:No different than normal.,c:Closer to the car ahead than normal.
note: On slippery roads, your tires have less traction and it takes longer to stop. You should increase your following distance so you have more space and time to brake gently and avoid skids or rear-end collisions.

question: How can you reduce the chance of hydroplaning in heavy rain?
options: a:Turn off your ABS system to improve traction.,b:Apply brakes hard as soon as the vehicle begins to skid.,c:Slow down and drive at a reduced speed for conditions.,d:Drive at the posted speed limit regardless of rain.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water and lose contact with the road. The most effective way to reduce this risk is to slow down and drive at a speed that matches the wet conditions, especially in heavy rain or standing water.

question: When must you show proof of insurance to an officer?
options: a:If stopped for a citation or involved in a collision.,b:Only if you are involved in a collision.,c:Only when stopped and cited.
note: You are required to carry proof of financial responsibility (usually insurance) and show it to a law enforcement officer when requested, such as when you are stopped for a traffic violation or involved in a collision.

question: Traffic control devices used in construction and maintenance areas are what color?
options: a:Yellow.,b:Blue.,c:Orange.,d:Red.
note: Orange signs and devices are used in construction and maintenance zones. When you see orange cones, barrels, or signs, slow down, stay alert, and be prepared for workers, lane shifts, and changing road conditions.

question: When a bicyclist is making a left turn, which lane position may they legally use?
options: a:They may use the left lane when turning left.,b:They may cut through all lanes at once.,c:They must always wait on the side of the road.
note: Bicyclists generally have the same rights and duties as drivers of motor vehicles. When making a left turn, a bicyclist may legally move into and use the leftmost lane or appropriate turn lane, just as a car would, to complete the turn safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign, what must drivers be prepared to do?
options: a:Yield only to vehicles on the right.,b:Slow but never stop.,c:Yield the right-of-way to cross traffic close enough to cause conflict.
note: A yield sign means you must slow down, be ready to stop, and give the right‑of‑way to any traffic (including pedestrians) that is close enough to create a conflict. You may proceed only when it is safe and you will not interfere with cross traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you enter a roundabout, to whom must you yield?
options: a:Only to pedestrians and bicyclists.,b:Only to vehicles already in the roundabout.,c:Both to any crossing pedestrians and bicyclists and to vehicles already in the roundabout.
note: When approaching a roundabout, you must yield to pedestrians and bicyclists who are crossing the entry or exit lanes, and you must also yield to all vehicles already circulating within the roundabout. Enter only when there is a safe gap in both pedestrian/bicycle traffic and vehicle traffic.

question: Which substances can impair your driving ability?
options: a:Tranquilizers,b:Vitamins and herbal teas exclusively.,c:Only illegal drugs,d:Only alcohol and narcotics
note: Driving can be impaired by many substances, including alcohol, illegal drugs, and numerous prescription and over‑the‑counter medications such as tranquilizers, pain relievers with codeine, and some antihistamines. You must always check medication warnings and avoid driving if a drug can make you drowsy, slow your reactions, or affect your judgment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If several vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.,b:The driver turning left proceeds first.,c:The largest vehicle goes first.,d:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two or more vehicles arrive at about the same time, each driver must yield to the vehicle on their right. This rule helps determine who goes first when there are no signs or signals.

question: If a vehicle has a two-part seat belt system, how should it be used?
options: a:Remove the shoulder portion if it’s uncomfortable.,b:Wear both the lap belt and shoulder belt together.,c:Use the shoulder belt alone without the lap belt.,d:Use only the lap belt for comfort.
note: Both lap and shoulder belts must be worn together for proper protection; using one part alone greatly reduces safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are continuously being passed on both sides while driving in the center lane of an expressway, what should you do?
options: a:Move to the lane on your right.,b:Stay in the center lane.,c:Move to the lane on your left.,d:Slow to the minimum speed limit.
note: On multi-lane highways, stay in the right lanes unless passing or preparing for a left turn; if traffic passes frequently on both sides, move right when safe.

question: If a school bus ahead in your lane is stopped with red lights flashing, what must you do?
options: a:Slow to 25 mph and pass cautiously.,b:Proceed if the bus is on the opposite side of a divided highway.,c:Stop and remain stopped while the red lights are flashing.,d:Stop only until you believe all children have exited the bus.
note: When a stopped school bus uses flashing red lights you must stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing; you do not need to stop if the bus is on the opposite side of a divided highway.

question: How must you respond when a pedestrian using a guide dog or carrying a white cane is crossing the street?
options: a:Tell them the safest path to cross.,b:Honking is permitted to speed them up.,c:Always yield the right-of-way to the pedestrian.,d:Proceed if they wait for you to pass.
note: Blind pedestrians using a cane or guide dog always have the right-of-way and must be yielded to.

question: What does a flashing red traffic light at an intersection mean?
options: a:The light is about to turn green so prepare to go.,b:Proceed without stopping if no cars are visible.,c:The same as a yield sign — slow and yield.,d:The same as a stop sign — come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.
note: A flashing red light requires a full stop, yielding to traffic and pedestrians, then proceeding when safe.

question: Blue traffic signs provide information about:
options: a:Regulatory instructions.,b:Construction and maintenance.,c:Motorist services such as rest areas, gas, food, lodging, or hospitals.,d:Mileage information and distances.
note: Blue traffic signs are service signs. They guide drivers to motorist services such as rest areas, gas stations, food, lodging, and hospitals. When you see a blue sign, look for information about nearby facilities that support drivers and travelers.

question: Which statement about alcohol and driving is true?
options: a:If you can walk in a straight line,b:Alcohol impairs judgment,c:Being under the legal BAC limit means you are not impaired.,d:Alcohol only affects coordination
note: Alcohol impairs judgment, decision‑making, and reaction time, even at low blood alcohol concentrations. You can be unsafe to drive even if you feel fine or are under the legal BAC limit, because your ability to assess risk and respond to hazards is already reduced.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before entering a curve?
options: a:Brake hard while turning.,b:Reduce your speed.,c:Increase your speed to maintain momentum.,d:Activate your turn signal.
note: You should slow down before entering a curve so your vehicle is at a safe, stable speed as you turn. Braking hard while already in the curve can cause skidding or loss of control, especially in poor conditions. Enter the curve at a controlled speed and then gently accelerate as you exit if needed.

question: While driving in a construction zone, you should:
options: a:Slightly increase your speed to pass quickly.,b:Expect workers to yield to motorists.,c:Expect the unexpected and be prepared to slow down or stop as directed by work‑zone signs and flaggers.
note: In construction zones, conditions can change quickly: lanes may shift, workers and equipment may be close to traffic, and speeds are often reduced. You should expect the unexpected, slow down, obey all work‑zone signs and flaggers, and be prepared to stop or change lanes safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which is NOT a safe practice on the interstate?
options: a:Slower traffic keeping to the right.,b:If you miss your exit, continue to the next exit.,c:Changing lanes without signaling.
note: On interstates, safe practices include keeping slower traffic to the right and continuing to the next exit if you miss yours instead of stopping or backing up. Changing lanes without signaling is not safe because other drivers need advance warning to adjust their speed or position and avoid collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parallel parking, how far from the curb should your wheels be?
options: a:Directly on the curb for stability.,b:Within two feet of the curb.,c:Within one foot of the curb.,d:Within three feet of the curb.
note: When parallel parking, your wheels should be parallel to and within about one foot of the curb. This keeps you out of the traffic lane while avoiding contact with the curb, which can damage your tires or wheels.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Should you always drive slower than the surrounding traffic?
options: a:Yes — it is a good defensive driving technique to drive well under the flow of traffic.,b:No — driving excessively slow can block traffic and be dangerous.,c:Yes — always safer to drive slower than others.
note: You must not drive so slowly that you block or interfere with normal traffic flow, unless it is necessary for safety or required by law. Driving much slower than surrounding traffic can cause sudden lane changes and rear-end collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At what speed should you travel?
options: a:At the speed limit regardless of conditions.,b:At the same speed as surrounding vehicles.,c:At a speed appropriate for the road and weather conditions.
note: You must never drive faster than is safe for current conditions, even if that is below the posted speed limit. Adjust your speed for rain, fog, traffic, curves, and road surface so you can stop safely if needed.

question: On a multilane road, a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:
options: a:Passing is prohibited from both directions.,b:Passing is permitted from both directions.,c:Passing is permitted only from the side next to the dashed line.
note: A dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line means only the traffic on the dashed side may cross the center line to pass when it is safe. Traffic on the solid-line side must not cross to pass.

question: Driving defensively includes which of the following actions?
options: a:Focusing only on the vehicle directly in front of you.,b:Keeping your eyes moving to scan for hazards.,c:Leaving a fixed stare down the road.
note: Defensive driving means constantly scanning the road ahead, to the sides, and behind you. By keeping your eyes moving, you can spot hazards early and have more time to react safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn at an intersection, to whom must you yield?
options: a:Oncoming traffic must yield to you.,b:You must yield to oncoming traffic and to pedestrians.,c:Pedestrians must yield to left-turning vehicles.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming vehicles that are going straight or turning right, and to pedestrians in any crosswalk you are turning across. Wait until there is a safe gap in oncoming traffic and the crosswalk is clear before completing your turn.

question: If you encounter an aggressive driver, what is the safest response?
options: a:Challenge them.,b:Get out of their way.,c:Follow closely to report them.,d:Speed up to get away.
note: With an aggressive driver, your goal is to avoid conflict and reduce risk. Do not challenge, block, or follow them. Safely create space by slowing slightly, changing lanes, or letting them pass, and focus on staying calm and out of their way.

question: If dust or smoke reduces visibility, what should you do to improve your visibility to others?
options: a:Turn on your headlights.,b:Turn on parking lights only.,c:Stop immediately in the roadway.,d:Use emergency flashers only.
note: In dust, smoke, or similar low-visibility conditions, turn on your low-beam headlights so others can see you more easily. Do not stop in a traffic lane unless absolutely necessary; if you must stop, pull completely off the roadway where it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane should you make a left turn when turning from a one-way street?
options: a:From the lane nearest the right curb.,b:From the lane nearest the left curb.,c:From any lane as long as you signal.,d:From the lane nearest the center of the street.
note: On a one-way street, a left turn should be made from the lane closest to the left curb, unless signs or lane markings direct otherwise. Begin and end your turn in the first legal lane going in your new direction to stay predictable and safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When traffic is merging into your freeway lane, what should you do?
options: a:Always maintain your lane position and speed.,b:Assert your right-of-way by accelerating.,c:Make room for the merging traffic if you can do so safely.,d:Brake hard to force them to stop.
note: When traffic is merging onto the freeway, help keep traffic flowing smoothly by making room if it is safe: adjust your speed slightly or change lanes to allow them to enter. Even though through traffic usually has the right-of-way, cooperating reduces the risk of sudden braking and collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle moving in the same direction, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: a:After about three seconds.,b:When you are one car length ahead of the passed vehicle.,c:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,d:When you can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.
note: After you pass another vehicle, don’t move back into the right lane until you can see both of that vehicle’s headlights in your inside rearview mirror. This shows you have enough space and won’t cut them off. Before moving back, signal and quickly check your blind spot to be sure the lane is clear.

question: Why should you use headlights during rain, snow, or fog?
options: a:To keep your engine warm.,b:To warn others of bad weather conditions.,c:So other drivers can see your vehicle.
note: Use your headlights in rain, snow, or fog so other drivers can see you more easily. In many states, the law requires headlights whenever your windshield wipers are on, and you should use low beams in fog or heavy precipitation so the light doesn’t reflect back and reduce your visibility.

question: When must you yield to a pedestrian?
options: a:Only when traffic signals favor the pedestrian.,b:Only when they wave you across.,c:At all times to avoid striking them.,d:Only if they are inside a marked crosswalk.
note: You must always do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian, even if they are crossing illegally. Drivers are required to yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and when they are in the path of your vehicle. Slow down, be prepared to stop, and give pedestrians the right-of-way whenever needed to prevent a collision.

question: When passing a motorcycle, what must you do?
options: a:Pass very closely to reduce wind effects.,b:Blow your horn to make the motorcycle move to the shoulder.,c:Stay in the right lane as much as possible and share a lane with the motorcycle.,d:Have your vehicle entirely in the left lane before and during the pass (give the motorcycle a full lane).
note: When passing a motorcycle, treat it like any other vehicle and give it a full lane. Move completely into the left lane before and during the pass and do not share the lane or crowd the rider. Return to your lane only when you can do so safely with plenty of space.

question: If a green light changes to yellow while you are already in the intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Continue moving and clear the intersection safely.,b:Accelerate to exit quicker.,c:Stop immediately in the intersection.
note: If the light turns yellow after you have already entered the intersection, continue through and clear the intersection safely. Do not stop in the middle of the intersection, and do not accelerate aggressively; just proceed at a safe, steady speed.

question: What is the only proven method to remove alcohol from your system?
options: a:Allow time for your body to metabolize the alcohol.,b:Drink strong coffee to sober up.,c:Take a cold shower.,d:Exercise vigorously to sweat it out.
note: Allowing time for your body to metabolize the alcohol is the only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC). Your liver needs time to process alcohol, and nothing speeds this up—not coffee, cold showers, exercise, or food. Those things might make you feel more awake, but they do not make you less impaired for driving.

question: A broken yellow centerline indicates:
options: a:You must stay in your lane at all times.,b:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,c:Both lanes of traffic are going in the same direction.,d:Passing is not permitted.
note: A broken yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions and allows passing on the left when it is safe and the way ahead is clear. You must still check for oncoming traffic, ensure you have enough space to pass, and obey any additional signs or markings that may restrict passing.

question: If the roadway ahead is flooded, what is the correct action?
options: a:Drive only in the center of the roadway.,b:Slam on the brakes and cross quickly.,c:Turn around and find another route; do not drive through flooded areas.
note: If the roadway ahead is flooded, you should always turn around and find another route. Even a small amount of moving water can sweep a vehicle away, and standing water can hide deep holes, debris, or road collapse. Because you cannot judge depth or current accurately from the driver’s seat, the safe choice is never to drive through floodwater.

question: Which lights should you use to improve visibility in rain or fog?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.
note: In rain, fog, snow, or sleet, use low beam headlights. Low beams aim light down toward the road and reduce glare. High beams reflect off moisture droplets in the air and can bounce back into your eyes, making it harder to see and making it harder for other drivers to see.

question: Which lights should you use as daylight fades to make your vehicle more visible?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Emergency flashers.,c:Low beam headlights.,d:Parking lights only.
note: As daylight fades, you should turn on your low beam headlights so other drivers can see you and you can see the road clearly. Low beams are appropriate for normal traffic conditions. High beams are reserved for dark, open roads with no oncoming traffic or vehicles directly ahead, and parking lights or flashers are not a substitute for proper headlights while driving.

question: When changing lanes, which action is prohibited?
options: a:Checking blind spots by looking over your shoulder.,b:Attempting to pass or change lanes within an intersection.,c:Signaling before initiating the lane change.,d:Checking for vehicles already in the lane you want to enter.
note: You must never change lanes or pass while you are in an intersection because traffic and pedestrian movements are more complex there. A safe lane change requires signaling, checking mirrors, and looking over your shoulder to clear blind spots before moving into the next lane.

question: When used on roadways, bicycles are legally considered:
options: a:Hazards.,b:Vehicles.,c:Dangerous objects.
note: On the road, bicycles are treated as vehicles. Cyclists generally must obey the same traffic signals, signs, and right‑of‑way rules as drivers, and drivers must treat bicycles as legitimate traffic, giving them space and yielding when required.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn, which action should you avoid?
options: a:Slowing down before the turn.,b:Signaling to alert other drivers.,c:Checking for pedestrians.,d:Swinging too wide into another lane.
note: When turning right, stay in your lane and turn into the nearest legal lane. Swinging wide can place you in another lane unexpectedly and put you in the path of vehicles beside you or oncoming traffic. Always slow appropriately, signal, and check for pedestrians and other road users before turning.

question: Yellow centerlines on the roadway separate:
options: a:Bicycle lanes from traffic lanes.,b:Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.,c:All carpool lanes from regular lanes.,d:Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
note: Yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions on two‑way roads. They mark the center of the roadway. White lines, not yellow, are used to separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction, such as on one‑way streets or multi‑lane roads.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should a driver view right-of-way rules while driving?
options: a:Assume all drivers will obey right-of-way rules exactly.,b:Assume most drivers obey the rules so you needn't worry.,c:Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way to avoid collisions.
note: Right‑of‑way rules help organize traffic, but you should never insist on your right‑of‑way if it could lead to a collision. Always be ready to yield, even when you are legally entitled to go, to avoid crashes caused by other drivers’ mistakes or inattention.

question: When parking next to a curb, when should you signal?
options: a:When pulling next to or away from the curb.,b:Only when pulling away from the curb.,c:Only when pulling next to the curb.
note: You must signal any time you move toward or away from the curb so other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians know you are entering or leaving the traffic lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: May you drive off the traveled roadway onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle?
options: a:If there are two or more lanes in your direction.,b:If the vehicle ahead is turning left.,c:Under no circumstances.
note: You may not drive onto the shoulder or off the main-traveled portion of the roadway to pass another vehicle; passing must be done within a proper lane on the roadway.

question: In bad weather, what driving technique is recommended?
options: a:Drive in a low gear at all times.,b:Steer off the road at the first sign of trouble.,c:Steer and brake smoothly.,d:Brake hard to stop quickly.
note: In bad weather, use smooth steering and gentle braking to maintain traction; sudden or hard braking and sharp steering can cause skids on wet, icy, or slippery roads.

question: Which of the following is true about crosswalks?
options: a:They are always unmarked.,b:They are always indicated by pavement markings.,c:They may be either marked with paint or unmarked and both are legal crosswalks.
note: A crosswalk can be painted (marked) or exist legally at an intersection even without paint (unmarked); drivers must yield to pedestrians in both types of crosswalks.

question: When parking uphill with a curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Keep the front wheels straight.,b:Turn the wheels away from the curb.,c:Turn the wheels toward the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels away from the curb so if the vehicle rolls, the front tire will hit the curb and stop the car from rolling into traffic.

question: How does driver fatigue affect your crash risk?
options: a:Increase errors in speed and distance judgment.,b:Cause you to fall asleep at the wheel and crash.,c:Help you make faster decisions.,d:Only lead to minor delays.
note: Fatigue makes you less alert, slows your thinking, and can even cause you to fall asleep while driving. It also harms your judgment of speed and distance, so you are more likely to make mistakes and be involved in a crash.

question: Reaction time is slower after which activity?
options: a:Working hard at a job.,b:Drinking alcohol.,c:Exercising regularly.,d:Sleeping well.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows your brain and body. After drinking, your reaction time is slower, your judgment is poorer, and your coordination is reduced, which greatly increases crash risk.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal indicate for drivers turning in that direction?
options: a:You do not need to signal when turning.,b:Prepare to stop and yield; the green arrow protection is ending.,c:You must stop immediately and remain stopped.,d:Speed up to complete your turn before it changes.
note: A solid yellow arrow means the protected green arrow is ending. You should prepare to stop if you can do so safely and be ready to yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, because your protected turn is about to end.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement edge, what is the correct way to re-enter the roadway?
options: a:Stop and wait for help.,b:Turn back onto the roadway immediately.,c:Slow down, keep control, and gently steer back onto the pavement when it is safe.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, stay calm and keep a firm grip on the wheel. Ease off the accelerator, slow down gradually, check for traffic, and when the car is under control, gently steer back onto the pavement. Do not jerk the wheel or suddenly swerve back onto the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Facing a green light with pedestrians in the intersection, what must you do?
options: a:Proceed because you have the green light.,b:Speed through before pedestrians finish crossing.,c:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.,d:Honk to let pedestrians know to clear the crosswalk.
note: Even on green, yield to pedestrians already in the intersection; drivers must yield when turning on a steady green.

question: If you've had several beers, what actually reduces the effects of alcohol?
options: a:Taking a cold shower.,b:Drinking several cups of coffee.,c:Waiting several hours for the body to metabolize it.
note: Only time will reduce alcohol concentration; cold showers or coffee do not speed alcohol elimination from your system.

question: Alcohol acts as which type of substance on the body?
options: a:Neither a stimulant nor a depressant.,b:A depressant that slows bodily and nervous system functions.,c:A stimulant that increases alertness.
note: Alcohol is a central nervous system depressant. It slows brain and body functions, including reaction time, coordination, and judgment. Even small amounts can reduce your ability to drive safely. It does not act as a stimulant, even if some people briefly feel more talkative or energetic.

question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?
options: a:They do not follow the same rules as motor vehicles.,b:A motorcycle can stop much faster than a standard vehicle.,c:They brake more slowly than cars.
note: Motorcycles are lighter and can often stop more quickly than larger vehicles. If you follow too closely, you may not have enough time or space to react if the motorcycle brakes suddenly, increasing the risk of a rear-end collision. Always leave extra following distance behind motorcycles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How do stopping distances and collision severity change with vehicle speed?
options: a:They decrease as speed increases.,b:They are unaffected by speed.,c:Both increase as vehicle speed increases.
note: As speed increases, both your stopping distance and the severity of any collision increase. You need more distance to perceive a hazard, react, and bring the vehicle to a stop. Higher speed also means more impact force in a crash, which greatly raises the chance of serious injury or death.

question: If you see a pedestrian using a guide dog or holding a white cane, you should:
options: a:Honk to let them know you are there.,b:Yield the right-of-way to them.,c:Expect them to yield to you.
note: A person using a white cane or a guide dog is blind or visually impaired and has the right-of-way. You must slow or stop as needed and allow them to cross safely. Do not honk, which can confuse or startle them. Proceed only after they have safely cleared your path.

question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol or drugs?
options: a:Only coordination is affected.,b:None of the above.,c:Both alertness and coordination are impaired.,d:Only alertness is affected.
note: Alcohol and many drugs affect multiple driving abilities at the same time, including alertness, coordination, reaction time, and judgment. Because both alertness and coordination are impaired, you cannot safely control the vehicle or respond quickly to hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you follow the directions of a school crossing guard?
options: a:Only if there are children present.,b:At all times while they are directing traffic.,c:Only if police are also present.,d:Only during school hours
note: School crossing guards have legal authority to direct traffic in school zones. You must obey their instructions any time they are actively directing traffic, regardless of whether children or police are present or whether it is during official school hours.

question: How should you apply the gas pedal for safe acceleration?
options: a:Depress it quickly to get moving fast.,b:Tap it lightly in short bursts.,c:Press it slowly and smoothly.
note: Safe acceleration uses smooth, gradual pressure on the gas pedal. Pressing the pedal slowly and steadily helps maintain traction, prevents wheelspin, and gives you better control of the vehicle, especially on wet or slippery roads.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign, what must you do?
options: a:Always slow down but never stop.,b:Yield only to vehicles coming from your right.,c:Yield to cross traffic that is near enough to cause conflict.
note: A yield sign means you must be prepared to slow down or stop and let cross or merging traffic go first if they are close enough to be a hazard. You only proceed when it is clear and safe, even if that means coming to a complete stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you yield your legal right-of-way?
options: a:Never; always use your legal right-of-way.,b:Only when a police officer tells you to.,c:Often,d:Whenever it helps prevent a collision.
note: Having the legal right-of-way does not guarantee safety. You should yield your right-of-way whenever doing so can prevent a collision, because other drivers may make mistakes, misjudge gaps, or ignore traffic rules.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left at a corner, to whom must you yield?
options: a:No one; left turns have priority.,b:Pedestrians and oncoming vehicles with the right-of-way.,c:Only vehicles turning right.,d:Only vehicles approaching from the left.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming vehicles that are close enough to be a hazard and to pedestrians who are in or entering the crosswalk with the right-of-way. You may only complete your turn when it is safe and will not interfere with these road users.

question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk?
options: a:Only if the pedestrians first wave the driver on.,b:Only when traffic lights indicate a walk signal.,c:At all times when pedestrians are in the crosswalk.,d:Only if pedestrians are not distracted by devices.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians who are in a marked or unmarked crosswalk, slowing or stopping as needed so they can cross safely. Pedestrians do not need to signal drivers first, and drivers must yield even if there is no walk signal, unless a specific traffic control device clearly gives the right-of-way to vehicles.

question: When a school bus is stopped ahead to load or unload children with lights flashing, what must drivers do?
options: a:Slow down to 10 mph and proceed.,b:Change lanes and pass the bus cautiously.,c:Come to a complete stop until all the children have left the bus.,d:Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.
note: When a school bus is stopped with red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, drivers in most situations must stop and remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn. Children may cross unexpectedly, so you must not move until the bus’s signals show it is safe to proceed.

question: Alcohol acts as which type of substance on the central nervous system?
options: a:A depressant.,b:An antihistamine.,c:A stimulant.,d:A hallucinogen.
note: Alcohol is a central nervous system depressant. It slows brain activity, weakens judgment, and reduces coordination and reaction time, making it much more difficult to drive safely even at relatively low blood alcohol levels.

question: If parking facing uphill where there is no curb, how should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Turn the wheels away from the edge of the road.,b:Keep the wheels straight ahead.,c:Turn the wheels toward the edge of the road (right).
note: When parking uphill with no curb, turn your front wheels toward the edge of the road (to the right). If the vehicle rolls, it will move away from the traffic lane and off the roadway instead of rolling into traffic.

question: What actually removes alcohol from your body?
options: a:Wait; only time removes alcohol from the body.,b:Take a cold shower.,c:Do vigorous exercise to sober up.,d:Drink strong coffee.
note: Only time eliminates alcohol from your system; eating, coffee, showers, or exercise do not speed up alcohol metabolism.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about vehicle blind spots is correct?
options: a:Blind spots are eliminated by having one outside mirror on each side.,b:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,c:Blind spots can be fully seen using only the rearview mirrors.
note: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Large trucks and buses have much larger blind spots on all sides than passenger cars, especially on the right side and directly behind them. Because of this, you should avoid driving alongside or close behind large trucks where the driver may not see you.

question: What should you do to help prevent hydroplaning on wet pavement?
options: a:Slow down.,b:Use cruise control to keep constant speed.,c:Move to the shoulder as soon as it begins to rain.,d:Increase tire pressure immediately.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on a thin layer of water and lose contact with the road, usually at higher speeds. The best way to help prevent hydroplaning is to slow down on wet roads, especially during heavy rain or when water is standing on the pavement. Good tire tread and avoiding sudden steering or braking also help.

question: If a truck or bus is turning right and you also need to turn right, what should you do?
options: a:Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.,b:Wait until the truck or bus has completed its turn before you turn.,c:Turn quickly ahead of the truck or bus.
note: Large trucks and buses often need to swing wide or start a right turn from a lane to the left to safely complete the turn. Never try to squeeze between a large vehicle and the curb or rush ahead of it. Stay behind and wait until the truck or bus has fully completed its turn before you make your right turn.

question: What must you do when a traffic signal displays a steady red arrow?
options: a:Drivers may turn if no other traffic is present.,b:Traffic in the indicated lane must remain stopped and may not proceed in that direction.,c:Drivers may turn in the arrow's direction after making a complete stop.,d:Drivers may turn in the arrow’s direction immediately.
note: A steady red arrow means you must stop and you are not allowed to go in the direction the arrow points. You must remain stopped until the signal changes to a green arrow or green light that permits movement in that direction. Treat it like a red light specifically for that lane and direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two lanes are moving in the same direction and you are in the left lane while others pass on the right, what should you do if someone behind wants to go faster?
options: a:Drive onto the shoulder briefly to let them pass.,b:Move into the right lane when it is safe to do so.,c:Stay in the left lane to avoid impeding traffic.,d:Brake sharply to signal them to pass.
note: On multi-lane roads, the left lane is generally for passing and the right lane is for through traffic. If vehicles are passing you on the right or a faster vehicle approaches from behind, you should safely move into the right lane when there is a clear gap. Never drive on the shoulder or brake sharply to communicate with other drivers, as these actions are unsafe and can cause collisions.

question: Under South Dakota's GDL program, how long must a teen hold an instruction permit before applying for a restricted minor's permit if they have NOT completed driver education?
options: a:90 days,b:180 days,c:275 days,d:1 year
note: In South Dakota, the instruction permit must be held for at least 275 days (or 180 days if an approved driver education course is completed) before moving to the restricted minor's permit phase.

question: On South Dakota roads with a speed limit of 35 mph or more, you must stay at least how many feet behind a snowplow with active flashing lights?
options: a:100 feet,b:200 feet,c:300 feet,d:500 feet
note: South Dakota law requires drivers to stay at least 200 feet behind any snowplow operating with its red or amber lights flashing on roads with a speed limit of 35 mph or higher.

question: Under South Dakota's Move Over law, when approaching a stopped vehicle displaying emergency signals on a two-lane highway, you must slow to:
options: a:The posted speed limit,b:At least 10 mph below the posted limit,c:At least 20 mph below the posted limit,d:15 mph
note: When approaching a stopped vehicle displaying emergency or warning signals on a two-lane highway, you must slow down to at least 20 mph below the posted speed limit (or 5 mph if the limit is 20 mph or less).

question: What is the minimum auto liability insurance coverage required for all motor vehicles registered in South Dakota?
note: South Dakota requires motor vehicle liability insurance coverage of 25/50/25: $25,000 for bodily injury per person, $50,000 for bodily injury per accident, and $25,000 for property damage.
